subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool-execution dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in tools, plugin tools, client tools, hooks, and delegated tool paths?
rationale: Automation can prove the feature gap, but cannot safely choose the product/security boundary for a trusted no-side-effects mode or decide whether a process-global CLI-only design is acceptable.

options.title: Design request-scoped dry-run
options.body: Specify the request-scoped runtime contract first, then implement an additive mode with redacted previews across built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, hook, and delegated-tool paths.

options.title: Defer to broader safe modes
options.body: Keep this issue open until the Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent-mode design chooses the shared vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Keep only command-specific dry-runs plus documented sandbox and tool-policy controls if maintainers decide global preview would be too easy to mistake for a full sandbox.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the request-scoped runtime contract first, then implement an additive mode with redacted previews across built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, hook, and delegated-tool paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The product/security boundary is closest to the original and repeated tool-execution hook ownership shown in history.
